sections.title: Objective type questions (2 parts of 1 mark, or 4 parts of ½ mark).

questions.q: Complete the sentence: Monsoons are not equally distributed. Coastal areas like Kerala, West Bengal and Odisha receive ____ rainfall, whereas interior regions like Haryana and Madhya Pradesh receive ____ rainfall.
questions.answer: heavy; less (low)

questions.q: Complete the sentence: The word 'Monsoon' is derived from the Arabic word ____, which means ____.
questions.answer: Mausim; season

questions.q: Answer in one word: (I) As the monsoon winds come from the south-west, which state do they strike first? (II) What is the hot, humid weather in the northern plains in October called?
questions.answer: (I) Kerala (II) October heat

questions.q: Answer briefly: (a) Why does Meghalaya receive more than 200 cm of rainfall per year? (b) Why does Rajasthan receive less than 60 cm of rainfall per year?
questions.answer: (a) The moist Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon is trapped by the funnel-shaped Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills and forced to rise, giving very heavy rain. (b) The Arabian Sea branch blows parallel to the Aravallis, so nothing makes it rise, and the Bay branch is nearly dry by the time it reaches Rajasthan.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: The violent thunderstorms of West Bengal in the hot season are called ____, and the crops sown with the arrival of the monsoon are called ____ crops.
questions.answer: Kaal Baisakhi; kharif

questions.q: True or False: (a) In winter the winds blow from land to sea, so most of India is dry. (b) The Deccan plateau east of the Western Ghats receives heavy rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch.
questions.answer: (a) True (b) False — it is a rain-shadow area and receives less rain.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the meaning of 'mango showers'.
questions.answer: (1) Towards the close of the summer season, pre-monsoon showers are common, especially in Kerala and Karnataka. (2) Hence, for most part of the country, it is a dry season. They help in the early ripening of mangoes, and are often referred to as ‘mango showers’.

questions.q: Explain any two features of the monsoon in India.
questions.answer: (1) Few days later they were surprised to see a news headline that monsoons are coming on time. They are irregular in nature affected by different atmospheric conditions i.e. due to regional climatic conditions. They help in the early ripening of mangoes, and are often referred to as ‘mango showers’. (2) Rainfall is unequal — coastal areas like Kerala and West Bengal get heavy rain while interior regions get less; the sudden heavy onset is called the 'burst of the monsoon'.

questions.q: Differentiate between weather and climate.
questions.answer: (1) Weather is the state of the atmosphere over a small area at a particular time and can change within a day. (2) is always for a large area like a country or a big region and generally it does not area for a long period of time (more than 30 years).Weatheris state of atmosphere over an area at any point of time.

questions.q: What are jet streams? How are they significant for change of weather in India?
questions.answer: (1) Upper air Currents: Besides surface winds, there are strong air currents called Jet streams which also influence the climate of India. These jet streams are a narrow belt of fast blowing winds located generally at 12,000 metre height above the sea level. (2) They bring western cyclonic disturbances along with them. These Jet streams shift northwards during summer season and blow in Central Asia. When monsoon winds enter from the coast, they give the maximum rain there.

questions.q: What type of weather prevails during October in different parts of India?
questions.answer: (1) (d) Retreating or Post Monsoon Season: October and November are the months of post (or retreating) monsoon season. (2) In the northern plains the weather is hot and humid ('October heat') but nights become pleasant by the end of the month; on the east coast cyclones from the Bay of Bengal bring heavy rain to Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What makes the Indian monsoon unique? Mention any three features.
questions.answer: (1) Monsoon refers to the seasonal reversal in the wind direction during a year. They are winter, summer, advancing monsoon and retreating monsoon. South to North and North-East and North-West. (2) They are irregular in nature affected by different atmospheric conditions i.e. due to regional climatic conditions. The monsoon tends to have ‘breaks’ in its rainfall which causes wet and dry spells. Human activities increase the amount of carbon dioxide, ChloroFloro Carbon (CFC) and other dangerous gases. (3) It begins with a sudden 'burst' on the Kerala coast and is unequally distributed, giving 80–90% of India's rain in four months (June–September).

questions.q: Why does the Tamil Nadu coast receive rainfall during winter while most of India remains dry? Explain two reasons.
questions.answer: (1) In winter the winds blow from land to sea so they are cold and dry. (2) During the winter season, North-East trade winds prevail over India. However, the Tamil Nadu coast receives winter rainfall due to these winds. A part of North-East trade winds blow over Bay of Bengal.

or.q: How does the wind system influence the climate of India during different seasons?
or.answer: (1) In winter the winds blow from land to sea so they are cold and dry. During the winter season, North-East trade winds prevail over India. However, the Tamil Nadu coast receives winter rainfall due to these winds. (2) The General direction of the wind during this season is from South-West to north-east.

questions.q: Describe any three factors affecting the climate of India.
questions.answer: (1) So in south of this latitude we find tropical climate and towards the north we find sub-tropical climate. For example, Andhra Pradesh would be hotter than Haryana. Broadly speaking parts lying south of the Tropic of Cancer receive more solar heat than those lying north of it. (2) Location:The places which are closer to equator have high temperature. Distance from the sea: The southern half of India is surrounded by sea from three sides: the Arabian Sea in the west, the Bay of Bengal in the east and the Indian Ocean in the south. For example the area of North India which is far away from the sea has extreme type of climate and the area of south India which is nearer to the sea has equable type of climate. In peninsular region, India’s rainfall decreases from coast to interior parts. (3) Mountains: the Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds and trap the monsoon; the Western Ghats cause heavy rain on their windward side. (Altitude, surface winds and jet streams also matter.)

questions.q: Explain any three reasons for the uneven distribution of rainfall in India.
questions.answer: (1) Relief: the Western Ghats and north-eastern hills force winds to rise and give heavy rain on windward sides, while leeward areas like the Deccan are rain-shadow areas. (2) On the other hand, in summer wind blow from sea to land bringing the moisture along with them from the sea and they cause wide spread rain in most part of the country. As we move from East to West in Northern plains, we observe that in central India rainfall decreases. When monsoon winds enter from the coast, they give the maximum rain there. (3) The Aravallis lie parallel to the Arabian Sea branch, so western Rajasthan gets very little rain.

questions.q: Describe any three main features of the hot weather season in India.
questions.answer: (1) From March to May temperatures rise in the plains, west and central India, and a low-pressure monsoon trough forms from Jaisalmer to Odisha. (2) In North- West India, afternoon dust storms are common. During summer, very hot and dry winds blow over North Indian plains. (i) The hot and dry wind blowing in the northern plain in the summer are called— (3) Local thunderstorms — Kaal Baisakhi in West Bengal — and pre-monsoon mango showers in Kerala and Karnataka occur.

questions.q: Describe any three characteristics of the cold weather season in India.
questions.answer: (1) This occurs mainly at Kerala coast where it reaches first. (a) Cold Weather Season: The duration of cold weather season is from December to February. The temperature decreases from the South to the North. Frost is common in the North and North- West India. (2) In winter the winds blow from land to sea so they are cold and dry. However, the Tamil Nadu coast receives winter rainfall due to these winds. A part of North-East trade winds blow over Bay of Bengal. (3) There is light rainfall in this region due to Western disturbances. Higher slopes of the Himalayas experience snowfall. The winter rainfall is very important for the cultivation of ‘Rabi’ crops.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the mechanism of the monsoon and describe the advancing south-west monsoon season.
questions.answer: (1) Mechanism: (2) In summer north-west India becomes very hot, creating a low-pressure monsoon trough from Jaisalmer to Balasore, while the Indian Ocean is cooler with high pressure. (3) Winds therefore blow from the ocean to the land from the south-west — a reversal of the winter north-east winds — carrying moisture. Advancing monsoon: (4) These moisture laden winds first hit at Andaman and Nicobar Islands in the last week of May and Kerala coast in the first week of June with violent thunder and lightning.This South-West monsoon that flows in to India brings about a major change in its weather. (5) The Arabian Sea Branch obstructed by Western Ghats gives heavy rainfall on the Western side of Western Ghats. When this branch crosses the Western Ghats and reaches the Deccan Plateau and parts of Madhya Pradesh, it gives less rainfall as it is a rain shadow region. (6) The Bay of Bengal branch strikes the north-east and West Bengal and turns west along the plains, rain decreasing westwards (Kolkata 120 cm, Delhi 56 cm). (7) The monsoon tends to have ‘breaks’ in its rainfall which causes wet and dry spells. We can see this decline is from 5°C to 8°C between mid June and mid July. Floods and droughts are hindrances in the economic growth of the nation as our economy is agro based economy.

questions.q: How are the seasons related to the socio-cultural and economic life of India? What is the impact of global warming?
questions.answer: (1) India's agro-based economy follows the seasons — kharif crops with the monsoon, rabi in winter, zaid at the end of winter. (2) Diet and clothing change with seasons — woollens and calorie-rich food in winter, juicy fruits and drinks in summer. (3) Festivals coincide with seasons and harvests: Makar Sankranti, Lohri, Pongal, Basant Panchami, Holi, Baisakhi, Onam, Dussehra, Durga Puja and Diwali. (4) Floods and droughts are hindrances in the economic growth of the nation as our economy is agro based economy. (5) Global warming — caused by CO2 and CFCs from industry, vehicles and deforestation — is disturbing the cycle of seasons. (6) Since about 70% of Indians depend on agriculture, rising temperatures and irregular rain can seriously harm food production and livelihoods.
